sentences.text: Hello, explorers!
Our planet is full of amazing animals, and some of them can do things that sound like magic.
Today, we are going on a journey across jungles, oceans, deserts, and icy lands to meet twenty-five of the most amazing animals on Earth.
Are you ready?
Let's begin our adventure!
Let's start in the ocean with the octopus.
Did you know an octopus has three hearts?
And its blood is not red, it's blue!
Each of its eight arms can taste and touch things all by itself.
Octopuses are so clever, they can open jars and squeeze through holes as small as a coin.
Next, we race to the African savanna to meet the cheetah, the fastest animal on land.
A cheetah can run about seventy miles per hour, as fast as a car on the highway!
Its long tail helps it turn quickly, like the rudder on a boat.
But cheetahs get tired fast, so they only sprint for a short time.
This tiny bird is the hummingbird.
Its wings move so fast that they hum, and that's how it got its name!
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than a thousand times every minute.
And here is something amazing: hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards!
Say hello to the elephant, the biggest animal that lives on land.
An elephant's trunk has around forty thousand muscles!
It uses its trunk like a hand, a nose, and a straw, all in one.
Elephants are also very smart and caring.
They remember their friends for many, many years.
Look up, way up!
The giraffe is the tallest animal in the world.
Its neck is super long, but guess what?
It has only seven bones in its neck, the same number as you!
A giraffe's tongue is dark purple and so long, it can even clean its own ears.
Now let's travel to icy Antarctica.
Emperor penguin dads are real heroes.
They hold their egg on top of their feet, under a warm flap of skin, for about two months in freezing winter storms.
During all that time, the dads don't eat at all, until the moms come back from the sea.
High in the rainforest trees lives the sloth.
Sloths move so slowly that tiny green plants called algae can grow on their fur!
That helps them hide in the leaves.
And sloths only climb down from their tree about once a week, to go to the bathroom!
These cute animals are sea otters.
When sea otters sleep on the water, they sometimes hold hands so they don't drift away from each other.
Isn't that sweet?
They even have a little pocket of skin under their arm, where they keep their favorite rock for cracking open shells.
Who, who, who is awake at night?
It's the owl!
An owl's eyes can't move around like ours.
So instead, owls can turn their heads almost all the way around.
Their soft feathers also help them fly in total silence, so they can sneak up on their dinner.
Hop, hop, hop!
Here comes the kangaroo from Australia.
When a baby kangaroo, called a joey, is born, it's only about the size of a jellybean!
The tiny joey crawls into its mom's pouch, where it stays warm and safe for months while it grows big and strong.
In the frozen Arctic lives the polar bear.
Polar bears look white, but here's a secret: their skin is actually black!
And their fur is not really white either.
Each hair is clear and hollow, and it just looks white in the sunlight.
The black skin helps them soak up the warm sun.
This smiling little creature is the axolotl, from the lakes of Mexico.
Axolotls have a real superpower.
If one loses a leg or its tail, it can grow a brand new one!
Scientists study axolotls to learn how bodies heal.
And look at that happy face!
Buzz, buzz!
Honeybees are small, but they are amazing workers.
When a bee finds yummy flowers, it flies back to the hive and does a special dance, called the waggle dance.
The dance tells the other bees which way to fly and how far to go to find the flowers!
Now let's meet the colorful chameleon.
Chameleons change their colors to show how they feel, and to warm up or cool down.
Their eyes can look in two different directions at the same time!
And their sticky tongue can shoot out longer than their whole body, to catch a bug in a flash.
Splash!
Dolphins are some of the smartest animals in the ocean.
Every dolphin has its own special whistle, a bit like a name, so its friends can call it.
And when dolphins sleep, only half of their brain rests at a time, so they can still swim and breathe.
Pretty in pink, it's the flamingo!
But did you know flamingos are not born pink?
Baby flamingos are gray and fluffy.
They turn pink from the food they eat, like tiny shrimp and algae.
And flamingos often rest standing on just one leg!
Shhh, this koala is sleepy.
Koalas can sleep up to twenty hours every day!
Their favorite food, eucalyptus leaves, gives them very little energy, so they rest a lot.
And here's a fun fact: koalas have fingerprints that look almost exactly like human fingerprints.
This rainbow animal is the mantis shrimp.
It's small, but it has one of the fastest punches in the animal world, fast enough to crack open hard shells.
Mantis shrimp can also see many more colors than people can.
Imagine all the colors they see!
The Arctic tern is the champion traveler of the animal world.
Every year, it flies from the top of the world all the way to the bottom, and back again.
That's about forty-four thousand miles each year!
Because of this trip, Arctic terns see more daylight than any other animal.
Deep in the forests of Africa live gorillas, our gentle animal cousins.
Gorillas share about ninety-eight percent of their DNA with people!
They live in families, and each night they build a cozy nest of leaves to sleep in.
Even though they are very strong, gorillas are peaceful and calm.
Now let's look through a microscope.
This is a tardigrade, also called a water bear.
It's so tiny, you can't see it with your eyes.
But water bears are super tough!
They can survive freezing cold, boiling heat, and scientists even sent them into outer space, and they survived!
When the pufferfish gets scared, it gulps water and puffs up like a spiky balloon.
But that's not all!
In Japan, scientists discovered a small pufferfish dad that draws beautiful circles in the sand on the sea floor, like a work of art, to impress a mom.
Flutter, flutter!
Butterflies are beautiful, and they are full of surprises.
Butterflies taste with their feet!
When they land on a leaf, they can tell if it's a good place to lay their eggs.
And every butterfly starts its life as a little caterpillar.
Tiny but mighty, it's the ant!
Some ants can carry things up to fifty times heavier than their own body.
That's like you lifting a car!
Ants work together as a team, and scientists think there are about two and a half million ants for every person on Earth!
And now, our biggest friend of all, the blue whale!
The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived, even bigger than the dinosaurs.
It can grow almost as long as three school buses in a row.
Its heart is as big as a small car, and its call is one of the loudest sounds in the animal world.
And that's the end of our journey!
From tiny water bears to the giant blue whale, our world is full of wonderful creatures.
Which animal was your favorite?
Tell us in the comments, and keep exploring, because nature is full of surprises.
See you next time, explorers!
